messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 router latency spike detected in us-west-2 (streaming paths). Auto-paging oncall. Investigate ASAP.

oncall-bot: Metrics: p95 -> 120ms, p99 -> 2.1s; streaming stall rate +340% vs baseline. Error rate for streaming sessions +4%.

alice: acked, joining bridge now. tagging @sam @nina @devops

sam: seeing the same in dashboards — router tail outliers correlate with a single load-balancer group (lb-usw2-a1). Heatmap shows disproportionate traffic to shard-7.

sam: quick numbers: total QPS normal, but shard-7 p99 = 3.8s, other shards p99 ~210ms.

nina: pulling router routing table and recent policy rollout changes. I see a weight bump from yesterday for lb-usw2-a1: `routing.weight_delta(lb-usw2-a1) = +0.18` at 03:10 UTC.

nina: also seeing a hotkey fanout normalized to shard-7 (many streaming sessions pinned). Could be a routing policy bug that prefers local affinity too strongly on new seed.

devops: if shard-7 is overloaded we can temporarily evict it from the balancer pool and let traffic redistribute. Propose: set weight=0 for lb-usw2-a1 and enable eager-fallback to euw2 for streaming routes.

sam: agree. Need to confirm there are available capacity headroom in euw2 and that model variants are compatible for streaming.

ryan: running quick safety checks now — listing capacity across regions

ryan: ```
$ rctl capacity list --region euw2 --kind streaming
region: euw2  available_slots: 120  reserved: 40
region: usw2  available_slots: 8    reserved: 200
```

ryan: euw2 has headroom, we can spill. Preparing to set weight to 0 on lb-usw2-a1. I'll do a staged change and monitor p99.

ryan: applying:
```bash
rctl balancer update --balancer lb-usw2-a1 --weight 0 --reason "mitigate hot-shard routing spike"
```

ryan: update: command returned ok, new effective weight=0. Watching metrics.

sam: immediate improvement on p99 for streaming routes: global p99 dropped from ~2.1s -> 480ms in 30s. shard-7 p99 down to 520ms. :thumbsup:

nina: still seeing some tail traces that show requests pinned to evicted shard via stale routing caches. We'll flush prefix cache on frontends to speed clearing.

alice: how are customers? @cust-success any alerts from customer-facing signals?

cust-success: getting 3 pager alerts from enterprise tenants A/B/C — short-lived timeouts and degraded streaming quality. Support is contacting affected accounts; first reply templates issued. No SLA breach yet flagged but monitoring.

devops: flushed caches across frontends (`/admin/cache/flush prefix=router-v2`) and triggered a graceful drain for shard-7 workers.

nina: confirmed stale entries clearing. tail traces now show requests hitting euw2 fallback. p99 stable ~380ms. Streaming stall rate trending down.

alice: good work. I'm going to call this a mitigated incident for now but keep the bridge open for postmortem notes and follow-ups. Assigning: postmortem owner = nina, mitigation owner = ryan, customer comms = cust-success.

sam: temporary root-cause hypothesis: routing rollout introduced an unexpected weight skew combined with hotkey-driven fanout that concentrated streaming sessions on a single balancer group. Need to audit the rollout and the policy code path that computes affinity seeds.

nina: agreed. Next immediate actions: 1) revert yesterday's routing weight bump for controlled rollouts (already set to 0), 2) run a canary of policy patch that fixes seed bias, 3) add guardrail to detect balancer group weight > 0.12 with high fanout.

ryan: leaving a flag for auto-fallback threshold so we don't need manual intervention next time. I'll open an infra-PR and link in thread.

cust-success: support will send an update to affected customers noting we mitigated routing skew and continued monitoring.

alice: bridge: marking incident as mitigated at 2026-03-15T18:20:10Z. We'll keep monitoring for an hour and then close if stable.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: p99 and streaming stalls reduced to baseline-based thresholds. Keep watch; create postmortem within 72h. ;incident:4187654321

alice: thanks team. Follow-up checklist in this thread: postmortem owner (nina), timeline + metrics (sam), infra PR (ryan), customer comms template (cust-success), alert tuning (devops).

nina: creating postmortem doc and will link to ops-docs once draft is ready.

ryan: PR: https://git.internal/rex/infra/pulls/4021 (wip) - adds fallback threshold + auto spill for region capacity.

cust-success: will draft customer note and share for review.

alice: closing bridge in 40m unless we see regressions. Good job. :party_popper:
